title: A codex seat can reach its MCP tools: the spawn surface stops handing it an approval policy of never
description:
GOVERNOR-FILED 2026-09-07 12:40Z, commissioning a producer that two rows are already parked on. NOT a plan — an architect owns the plan.

THE MEASURED DEFECT, reported independently by worker-ca28be90 (task-117a3cd9, comment-0daf2fcd / comment-e71b5ece / comment-cab9a6e3) and worker-b1872f24 (task-96957529 completion record):

A real `codex exec` seat spawns, registers, and is handed `MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never`. It therefore can never call `work_get_context`, and so can never reach `review_submit` or `work_release`. NO CODEX SEAT CAN DELIVER ANY NODE. Everything upstream of the MCP call works: the fresh-store lane comes up, the seed reaches `READY node.deliver@node-live-livecodex2105097`, the provider is chosen by the DURABLE SETTING (`project.set_agent_provider` -> HTTP 200 `AGENT_PROVIDER_SET`, `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` verified UNSET), and six durable `internal.wrapper.seat_start` rows carry `{"agentVersion":"codex-cli 0.153.4","provider":"codex"}` with live codex-shaped argv (PID 53332; node 40484 -> cmd 61832 -> codex).

NOT A QUOTA BLOCK, confirmed twice ~50 min apart: `codex exec "say hi"` EXIT 0, `Hi!`, codex 0.153.4. `mem:real-codex-limit-available-on-this-host` is SUPERSEDED — this host can no longer produce a real provider limit on demand.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING, codex-side not a moe bug, record it rather than fixing it here: `--ignore-user-config` silently downgrades `--sandbox workspace-write` to `read-only`. Controls measured: user-config -> workspace-write; +ignore-user-config -> read-only; +ephemeral -> read-only (ephemeral exonerated); danger-full-access -> honoured.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS RATHER THAN A DEPENDENCY EDGE: the findings sit on task-48932bec, which is already DONE, so naming it in blockedOnTaskIds would auto-unblock the waiters on a signal that fixes nothing. worker-ca28be90 said so explicitly and deliberately left blockedOnTaskIds empty.

WHAT IS PARKED ON THIS: task-117a3cd9 (BLOCKED 63m+, no deps and no resource, so nothing auto-unblocks it) and task-96957529 (QA-rejected at HEAD 205b1643 with 2 of 5 DoD clauses open — both of the open ones require a codex seat to actually deliver a node). Neither is a worker defect; QA and the workers agree on the facts and there is no "approve with notes". Both rows should be gated on this one rather than ping-ponging through reject cycles.

Recipe and reproduction detail: `mem:task-task-117a3cd9-handoff`. Read it before planning; do not re-derive the census.
definitionOfDone: A real `codex exec` seat spawned by the production wrapper completes an `mcp__moe__moe_work_get_context` call and the call's success is proven from the seat's own surface (its transcript or a durable `internal.wrapper.*` row), not from an author's intent or a scripted double.

The approval-policy value the wrapper passes to `codex exec` is asserted ON THE SPAWN SURFACE — the argv or the child's environment — with a control proving the previous value was `never`. A test that asserts the intended setting rather than the emitted argv does not discharge this.

A codex seat drives one node from READY to a recorded `review.submit` and `work_release`, and the landing sha is quoted. If the node cannot land for a reason OUTSIDE the MCP reachability defect, that reason is named and measured rather than the clause being narrowed.

The `--ignore-user-config` / `--sandbox` downgrade is recorded where the next reader will hit it (a docblock at the spawn site or a durable memory), with the four measured controls. Recording it is enough; fixing codex is out of scope.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim, plus whichever e2e lane covers the codex spawn surface. Any red is attributed by path and disclosed verbatim, never waived.
taskRails: This row owns the codex SPAWN SURFACE. It does not re-open task-48932bec (DONE) and does not edit the claude spawn path except where a shared helper forces it — if it does, say so and name the shared symbol.

Assert on the argv or the child environment, never on the setting you passed in. The shim/basename selector means a near-miss silently runs the claude branch (`mem:gotcha-codex-shim-basename-selects-the-provider-and-fails-silently`), and a claude seat reported as codex is the worst available outcome.

The codex seat carries its bearer in the child's own environment. Paste variable NAMES and never values into any comment or transcript — a raw env dump in a row comment publishes a credential that cannot be recalled.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE THE GAP AND THE BLAST RADIUS. No edits. Record verbatim: (a) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ tests/e2e/foundation/` — foreign dirt is noted and continued past; (b) `git grep -n 'ask-for-approval\|approval_policy\|bypass-approvals\|full-auto' -- apps/daemon/src` returning NOTHING, which is the defect: `codex exec` defaults its approval policy to `never` and the spawner never overrides it; (c) `sed -n '88,98p' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts` capturing today's exact codex argv; (d) `git show --stat 6dbdbe69` confirming sibling task-df64aa20 landed a TEST-SWEEP fix with zero production bytes, so it did NOT close this gap — do not treat that DONE row as the owner; (e) `git grep -ln '"--ignore-user-config"\|--skip-git-repo-check\|"--ephemeral"'` and record every CODE asserter (expect agent-spawner.test.ts, seat-exit-classifier.ts + its test, tests/e2e/foundation/codex-seat-loop.e2e.test.ts; .moe/ JSON and chat logs are not asserters), plus what `seat-exit-classifier` keys on — if it matches on argv shape, an added flag can change classification. Record the HEAD sha.

MEASURE THE KNOB BEFORE CHANGING ANY PRODUCTION BYTE — this is an empirical question and guessing it wastes a live drive. Against real `codex exec` 0.153.4 on this host, run a control table ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME, exactly as the existing sandbox controls were run, and record the full table with its commands. The question each control answers is NOT what the session banner prints but whether AN MCP TOOL CALL ACTUALLY COMPLETES — stand up a trivial local MCP server (or point at a throwaway daemon) and require a real tool call, because the banner has already been shown to disagree with argv on this exact surface. Tiers to measure, narrowest first: (i) a per-server trust / tool allow-list via `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.<knob>` — note the known negative, `disabled_tools=[]` pre-approves NOTHING; (ii) `-c approval_policy=<value>` and `--ask-for-approval <tier>`, expecting the non-interactive tiers to fail closed since `exec` has nobody to prompt; (iii) REPLACING `--ignore-user-config` with a per-seat EMPTY `CODEX_HOME`, which may close the sandbox downgrade in the same stroke — measure BOTH whether the MCP call completes AND whether `--sandbox workspace-write` survives; (iv) `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, recorded as the widest tier and shipped only if nothing narrower works. SAFETY: any control that readmits user config must run with the real board's MCP server unreachable — a bare `codex exec` on this host has been measured calling the operator's own moe server unprompted. Choose the NARROWEST tier that produces a completed MCP call, and say in the note why each narrower one failed.

CHANGE THE SPAWN SURFACE, narrowly. Apply the tier step 2 measured to the codex branch of `agent-spawner.ts` (the argv array at :88-97 and/or the child environment), and update the docblock at :68-79 to state what was measured, on which codex version and host, and why the narrower tiers were rejected — that block is already the record of this surface's measurements and is where the next reader will look. Do NOT touch the claude branch; if a shared helper forces a change there, stop and name the shared symbol (task rail 1). If the chosen tier widens the sandbox or readmits configuration, say so explicitly in the docblock as a security note rather than letting a flag land unexplained. Keep `agent-spawner.ts` under 400 lines.

ASSERT IT ON THE SPAWN SURFACE, WITH THE CONTROL DoD 2 DEMANDS. In `agent-spawner.test.ts`, update the EXACT-ARRAY arm at :280-290 (it will be red after step 3 — that redness is the point) and add an arm that pins the approval setting ON THE EMITTED ARGV OR THE CHILD ENVIRONMENT, never on the value passed in. The control is mandatory and is what makes the arm non-vacuous: prove that WITHOUT this change the effective policy is `never` — e.g. an arm asserting the old argv carried no approval setting at all, so a future edit that silently drops the flag goes red. Follow the file's existing credential discipline: argv names the bearer VARIABLE, and the secret must be absent from `file + args`. Update the `describe("keeps the codex spawn surface intact")` arms at :1421+ and, if step 1 found `seat-exit-classifier` keys on argv shape, its arms too. Verify each new arm by mutating the production surface until it goes red, then restore.

THE LIVE DRIVE — DoD 1 and DoD 3, and the only thing that proves this row worked. Use the recipe in `mem:task-task-117a3cd9-handoff` verbatim; do not re-derive it. Its two most expensive traps: the node spec's `workspace` must be a WINDOWS path (`pwd -W`; an msys `/tmp/...` string is invisible to the win32 daemon), and select codex by the DURABLE setting — `project.set_agent_provider` with `{"base":"","goalId":"","provider":"codex"}` and `expectedVersion: 0` (NOT null — null is refused INPUT_INVALID @ DECODE with empty `details`), leaving `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` UNSET or you are proving the fallback. Then: a real seat completes an `mcp__moe__moe_work_get_context` call, proven from the seat's own transcript or a durable `internal.wrapper.*` row — not from intent and not from a scripted double; and one node goes READY -> `review.submit` -> `work_release` with the landing sha quoted. READ THE OUTCOME FROM THE DURABLE LEDGER, never stdout or an exit code: `command_decisions.result_bytes` for `internal.wrapper.seat_start`, `domain_events` for the delivery. `LandingBaselineRecorded` is written BEFORE the seat runs — quoting its sha as a landing sha is a false completion claim. IF THE NODE CANNOT LAND for a reason outside the MCP defect — the read-only sandbox is the expected one — NAME AND MEASURE that reason; do not narrow the clause. Paste variable NAMES only, never values.

RECORD THE SANDBOX DOWNGRADE WHERE THE NEXT READER HITS IT — DoD 4. In the `agent-spawner.ts` docblock beside the flag, state the four measured controls verbatim: `--sandbox workspace-write` alone yields workspace-write; adding `--ignore-user-config` silently yields read-only with NO error; adding `--ephemeral` on top is still read-only, so `--ephemeral` is EXONERATED; and `danger-full-access` survives the flag. Say plainly that this is codex 0.153.4 behaviour and NOT a moe defect — the spawner passes the flag correctly — because reading "argv says workspace-write, banner says read-only" as a spawner bug is the obvious inference and it is false; the controls are the only thing separating them. If step 2's CODEX_HOME tier removed the downgrade, record that instead as the resolution and keep the controls as the history that justified the change.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Run each leg FOREGROUND and STANDALONE and read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — no `Test Files N passed` line means nothing ran. Legs, quoted verbatim with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (DoD 5's named leg), and the e2e lane covering the codex spawn surface — `pnpm test:e2e`, naming `tests/e2e/foundation/codex-seat-loop.e2e.test.ts` in the output. Repo-wide legs are a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: record failures at the merge-base and at HEAD, and the delta intersected with this row's owned paths must be EMPTY; disclose foreign red verbatim with its exact failing paths and never waive it. Then read your own diff as an attacker: does the new arm still fail if the approval flag is deleted from the argv — mutate and confirm red? Could a near-miss run the CLAUDE branch while still reporting codex? Is the bearer value absent from argv, from every test fixture, and from every note you wrote? Did the claude branch change at all? Is the chosen tier the narrowest that worked, and is any widening stated as a security note rather than buried in a flag? Confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only paths you own plus the step-1 foreign dirt, and report every touched path in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`.

comments.content:
PLANNING MEASUREMENT — the gap is open, plus one DoD tension the worker must not meet at step 5. HEAD, 2026-09-07.

1. THE SIBLING THAT LOOKS LIKE IT CLOSED THIS DID NOT. `task-df64aa20 "A codex seat plans and delivers over the real MCP wire"` is DONE and landed at 08:56Z, before this row was filed at 12:40Z, so the re-measure rail required checking it. `git show --stat 6dbdbe69` is a TEST-SWEEP fix with **zero production bytes** — `codex-journey-harness.ts`'s `spawnRecords()` swept the version PROBE in with the SEAT records, so the spawn-surface arm graded the wrong record. Its own message says "Fixed in the sweep, not the surface (task rail 3), zero production bytes." The approval defect is untouched. Do not read that DONE row as the owner.

2. THE DEFECT IS AN ABSENCE, ON ONE LINE. `agent-spawner.ts:88-97` builds the codex argv as exactly `exec`, `--ignore-user-config`, `--skip-git-repo-check`, `--ephemeral`, `--sandbox <role.sandbox>`, three `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.*` overrides, the roster args, `-`. `git grep -n "ask-for-approval\|approval_policy\|bypass-approvals\|full-auto" -- apps/daemon/src` returns NOTHING. `codex exec` defaults its approval policy to `never` and refuses an MCP tool call that requires approval, so `work_get_context` fails and nothing downstream of it is reachable.

3. **DoD 3 AND DoD 4 PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER — flagging it now rather than letting a live drive discover it.** DoD 4 says the `--ignore-user-config` sandbox downgrade need only be recorded ("fixing codex is out of scope"). But DoD 3 requires a seat to reach `review.submit` and `work_release`, and under the downgraded `read-only` sandbox the measured seat could not write a file at all ("File creation is prohibited by read-only filesystem permissions"; its verify died `rejected: blocked by policy`). **Clearing the approval gate alone will not deliver a node.** The plan's step 2 therefore measures both in one control table, because one change may close both: replacing `--ignore-user-config` with a per-seat empty `CODEX_HOME` would keep the host's config and its MCP servers out — which is the whole reason the flag exists — while letting `--sandbox workspace-write` survive. That is PLAUSIBLE, NOT PROVEN; step 2 measures it. If it does not hold, DoD 3's own escape clause applies: name and measure the blocking reason. The honest outcome is then a second row for the sandbox, not a quietly narrowed DoD.

4. THE KNOB IS AN EMPIRICAL QUESTION, so the plan measures before it edits. Control table, narrowest first: a per-server trust/allow-list `-c` knob (known negative: `disabled_tools=[]` pre-approves nothing — an empty disable-list is not an allow-list); `-c approval_policy=` / `--ask-for-approval` tiers, expected to fail closed since `exec` has nobody to prompt; the CODEX_HOME swap; and `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` as the widest tier, shipped only if nothing narrower works. Each control is graded on **whether an MCP tool call actually completes**, not on the session banner — banner and argv have already been measured disagreeing on this exact surface.

5. SAFETY CONSTRAINT ON THE CONTROLS. A bare `codex exec` on this host was measured picking up the operator's own config and calling the operator's REAL moe MCP server unprompted (`mcp: moe/moe.claim_next_task started/(completed)`). Any control that readmits user config must run with the board's MCP server unreachable, or it has touched the real board.

6. ARGV ASSERTERS, enumerated per the shape rail (a symbol grep alone is not sufficient): `agent-spawner.test.ts` holds an EXACT `toEqual` on the whole array at :280-290 plus a `describe("keeps the codex spawn surface intact")` block at :1421+; `seat-exit-classifier.ts` and its test reference the same flags; `tests/e2e/foundation/codex-seat-loop.e2e.test.ts` is the lane arm. All four are in the plan's paths. The exact-array arm WILL go red when the flag lands — that is the intended signal, and DoD 2's control is what keeps the updated arm non-vacuous.

Credential discipline (task rail 3) is carried into every step: the bearer rides `MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER` in the child's own environment; variable NAMES only in notes and comments, never values.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (a.k.a. yolo). REJECTED as the default answer: it removes the sandbox as well as the approval gate, so a code seat would run unconfined on the operator's host. It stays on the control table as the widest tier, not as the shipped setting.
(2) DROP `--ignore-user-config` so the host config's approvals apply. REJECTED on measured evidence: a bare `codex exec` on this host picks up the operator's own config AND CALLS THE OPERATOR'S REAL MOE MCP SERVER unprompted (it emitted `mcp: moe/moe.claim_next_task started/(completed)`). Readmitting user config lets a seat reach the real board. That is why the flag was added (agent-spawner.ts:73).
(3) THE ONE WORTH MEASURING FIRST — keep the host's config out by pointing a per-seat `CODEX_HOME` at an empty directory INSTEAD of `--ignore-user-config`. The spawner's own comment records that codex's help says auth still uses CODEX_HOME, so isolation by CODEX_HOME plausibly keeps the host's servers out while letting `--sandbox workspace-write` survive — which would close BOTH findings with one change. PLAUSIBLE, NOT PROVEN: step 2 measures it with controls rather than shipping it on the strength of this paragraph.
(4) A PER-SERVER TRUST / TOOL ALLOW-LIST via `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.<knob>`. Also on the control table. The measured negative is already known: `disabled_tools=[]` pre-approves NOTHING — an empty disable-list is not an allow-list.
(5) `--ask-for-approval on-request` or `on-failure`. Listed but expected to fail closed: `codex exec` is non-interactive, so there is nobody to answer a prompt. If a tier does work it must be proven by a completed MCP call, not by the banner.

planningNotes.risks:
DoD 3 AND DoD 4 PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER, AND THE WORKER MUST NOT DISCOVER THIS AT STEP 5. DoD 4 says the `--ignore-user-config` sandbox downgrade need only be RECORDED ("fixing codex is out of scope"). But DoD 3 requires a codex seat to drive a node to `review.submit` and `work_release` — and under the downgraded `read-only` sandbox the seat cannot write a file at all: the measured seat reported "File creation is prohibited by read-only filesystem permissions" and its verify died `rejected: blocked by policy`. So DoD 3 is UNREACHABLE while the downgrade stands, and clearing the approval gate alone will not deliver a node. This is why step 2 measures the CODEX_HOME isolation alternative in the same pass: one change may close both. If it does not, DoD 3's own escape clause applies — name and MEASURE the blocking reason rather than narrowing the clause — and the honest outcome is a second row for the sandbox, not a quietly weakened DoD.

A NEAR-MISS SILENTLY RUNS THE CLAUDE BRANCH. The shim/basename selector means a codex seat that misses the selector runs claude and reports as codex — the worst available outcome (`mem:gotcha-codex-shim-basename-selects-the-provider-and-fails-silently`, and task rail 2). Assert on the emitted argv or the child environment, never on the setting passed in.

CREDENTIALS. The codex seat carries its bearer in the child's OWN environment (`MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER`). Paste variable NAMES only — never values — into any comment, step note or transcript; a raw env dump in a row comment publishes a credential that cannot be recalled. The existing arm already pins this discipline: argv names the variable, and the test asserts the secret is absent from `file + args`.

NO `codex exec` ON THIS HOST IS SIDE-EFFECT-FREE if user config is readmitted — it reached the operator's REAL moe MCP server and called `claim_next_task` unprompted. Any control that drops `--ignore-user-config` must run with the board's MCP server unreachable or be treated as having touched the real board.

WIDENING IS A SECURITY CHANGE, NOT A CONFIG TWEAK. If the measured answer is `danger-full-access` or a bypass flag, say so plainly in the completion record with what it widens and why the narrower tiers failed. Do not ship the widest tier because it was the first that worked.
